summary: A voting day is told as a sequence: waited in line, went to work, came back and voted, then went out for the returns.
realLife: In 1860 Strong left a block-long line to attend a business meeting, came back at two and voted for Lincoln, then went downtown that night to the newspaper offices for the returns.
sources: House Divided, Dickinson College, George Templeton Strong's diary, election day 6 Nov 1860: https://hd.housedivided.dickinson.edu/node/34626
Emerging Civil War, Strong's election-day diary entries 1840 to 1872: https://emergingcivilwar.com/2020/11/03/this-momentous-day-presidential-elections-process-in-19th-century-nyc/
